review: Independent checkpoint verification of phase 2A and of proposal revision 1. Not final goal acceptance

summary.phase2A: The local guards are correct and the suite passes, 21 of 21. The baseline guard fails open in CI, which already runs pnpm check with CI=1, a shallow checkout and no FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE. It also fails open when git is unavailable even though a baseline is configured. Limitation 4 claims behavioural tests cover the refines that JSON Schema drops; only one refine is tested.
summary.proposal: F1–F17 and T1–T4 are all resolved. One new decision is defective: the tombstone register lives inside the database that a restore rolls back (medium). There are three smaller issues in the new decisions (rate windows, the actor key's foreign keys, replay after a role demotion), plus two documentation gaps.

phase2A_confirmed: Discovery finds 23 schemas: 22 in models.ts plus paise. calculations.ts and dates.ts export no Zod schema. Duplicate names throw (contract.ts:16-21). Coverage is checked both ways against the index.ts exports (contract.test.ts:60-67)
persistedContracts and the render options match scripts/backend/contracts.ts:6-7 exactly
The current-schema guard compares bytes against <CONTRACT_VERSION>.json. Keys are sorted at every depth, and non-finite values are refused (contract.ts:30-48; contract.test.ts:35-43)

Manifest guard: strict shape, semver, strictly increasing, ends at CONTRACT_VERSION, every listed file has its SHA-256, no unlisted files. The passing hash test confirms that 0.1.0.json hashes to 74914ca9… as manifest.json records
baselineProblems requires the baseline's entries as an ordered prefix and each file's recorded hash. It rejects the forged self-consistent pair (contract.test.ts:91-98)

planSnapshot validates history before checking semver, existence and ordering (snapshot-contract.ts:118-131). writeSnapshot uses wx for both files and an atomic rename. Importing the module does not run main() (invokedDirectly, :167-170)
The client graph from index.ts has no node: or built-in imports. contract.ts imports only zod and local modules
M1.1 restore: the session-start git status lists only package.json and src/index.ts as modified, so models.ts was unmodified at session start. contracts/ holds only manifest.json and 0.1.0.json

findings.reason: The guard fails open in CI. If FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE is unset, or empty (for example a '${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}' expression on a push event), it falls back to HEAD and local main. The existing CI job runs pnpm check with CI=1 on a shallow actions/checkout of the pull request merge ref, where no local main exists. main is skipped with only a diagnostic, and HEAD equals the working tree. A pull request that rewrites a merged snapshot and its manifest hash together, or resolves a parallel-lane version clash by keeping its own file, therefore passes. This contradicts 003 §8 (003:840-847) and T4's fail-closed decision (phase1-dispositions.md:333-339).
findings.fix: In gitBaselines, when env.CI is set (non-empty, not 'false' or '0') and the variable is unset or empty, throw 'FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE must be set in CI to the trusted base commit'. Merge this with PL-1's workflow change, or after it: set actions/checkout fetch-depth to 0, and set FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE to '${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}'. Otherwise every CI run goes red. Add mutation checks that mirror M2.3 and M2.4.

findings.reason: If 'git rev-parse --show-prefix' fails, the function returns no baselines before it looks at the variable. Causes include no .git directory, a git 'dubious ownership' refusal in a container, or no git binary. The test then passes with only a diagnostic, even when FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE is set. This contradicts phase2A.md:70: 'A configured ref that does not resolve is an error.'
findings.fix: Read the variable first. If it is set, or CI is set, and the prefix is null, throw. Keep the quiet skip only for local runs with no variable.

findings.reason: git() swallows every error and discards stderr. The baseline read treats any 'cat-file -e' failure as 'file absent': a missing object in a partial or shallow clone, an I/O error, and so on. A missing baseline manifest means 'first baseline' (:74), so a read error passes silently.
findings.fix: Tell absence apart from failure. For example, list files with 'git ls-tree -z --name-only <base> -- <path>' and throw on a non-zero exit, then use 'cat-file blob' only for listed files. Include stderr in the thrown message.

findings.reason: No test exercises the configured-baseline path (snapshot-contract.ts:103-106). Nothing shows a resolving ref, an unresolvable ref that throws, or an unrelated ref. The suite has only ever run the default HEAD-and-main branch.
findings.fix: Add tests. gitBaselines(contractsDir, {FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE: 'refs/heads/ar1-no-such-ref'}) throws /not a commit/. {FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE: 'HEAD'} returns one source labelled HEAD@…. After P2A-1, {CI: 'true'} throws, and so does {CI: 'true', FITLOG_CONTRACT_BASELINE: ''}.

findings.reason: Limitation 4 says 'Behavioural tests and fixture vectors catch the change itself.' Only the body-entry refine is tested, and only its reject case (calculations.test.ts:61). Nothing pins repsMin <= repsMax, deadline >= startDate, the IANA time-zone check (the snapshot renders timezone as {"type":"string"}) or the trim on name. Any of these can be weakened with no bump and no failing test. Three persisted contracts (days, instances, goal) carry refines that Postgres JSON Schema validation cannot express.
findings.fix:
Add a 'refinement vectors' test to contract.test.ts with the accept and reject boundary of each rule:
- repsMin == repsMax is accepted; repsMin > repsMax is rejected at path repsMax.
- deadline == startDate and null are accepted; an earlier deadline is rejected.
- 'Asia/Kolkata' is accepted; 'Mars/Phobos' is rejected.
- ' a ' parses to 'a'; '   ' is rejected.
- A notes-only body entry is accepted; an empty one is rejected.
Optionally, add an inventory test that counts the custom and overwrite checks per schema, so adding or removing a refine fails. Then correct the limitation text.

findings.reason: planSnapshot accepts any higher version. A schema change can therefore ship as a patch bump, but 003 §4.1 says a patch never changes the wire format within its line.
findings.fix: If the new version differs from the last one only in PATCH, and its schemas or persisted section differ from the last snapshot, refuse: 'a schema change needs a new compatibility line (MINOR before 1.0.0)'. Add a test.

findings.reason: The Node-free test scans only import specifiers. With types: ['node'], a client-reachable module can use Buffer, process or __dirname without an import, and neither the test nor tsc fails. Such code would break on Hermes.
findings.fix: Add tsconfig.client.json with 'types': [], files ['src/index.ts'] and no include, plus the same strict options. Run 'tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit' in the typecheck script.

findings.reason: The write path is untested. M1.4 shows only that planSnapshot refuses, so the wx refusal, the rollback after a failed rename, and the check after writing have never run. When the temporary file's wx fails with EEXIST, the catch block removes a manifest.json.<pid>.tmp that this run did not create. The rule that unlisted files block planning makes this practically unreachable. Concurrent runs can still lose a manifest append (limitation 6).
findings.fix:
Test writeSnapshot in a mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()) directory:
1. A clean write that verifies.
2. A second write that fails with EEXIST and leaves no temporary file.
3. A rename that fails (make manifest.json a directory) and leaves only the original files.
Remove the temporary file only if this run created it. Optionally, create a manifest.lock with wx around plan-and-write.

findings.reason: actors.erased_at is the purge tombstone register, but it sits inside the database whose backups it must override. A backup or point-in-time copy taken before an erasure has erased_at NULL for that user. 'Purge every account with erased_at set' then does nothing for exactly the accounts at risk, and the user is resurrected. This fails PRD §22.3 (PRD.md:1530-1531), AC30 (PRD.md:1797) and MB-7 box 2 (GOALS.md:663: 'restoring a pre-erasure snapshot … and replaying tombstones does not resurrect the user').
findings.fix: At erasure step 2, also append the tombstone (actor UUID and erased_at, no personal field) to a register outside every restorable database copy, for example a private ops Storage object or a separate ops project. Keep it at least as long as the longest backup expiry (≤90 days, PRD.md:1530). actors.erased_at stays as the in-database copy. PL-5's restore runbook imports the external register and purges every listed account before serving. MB-7's test replays from the external register. Note the external copy under R-4.

findings.reason: 'A rolled-back request does not count.' Every rejected v1 command or read raises PT<status>, which rolls the counter back. So 401, 403, 404, 409 and 422 responses are never counted. PRD §18.1 (PRD.md:1184) limits write requests to 120 a minute and 5,000 a day, and reads to 600 a minute. An authenticated client can send unlimited rejected writes, each of which takes the per-account lock.
findings.fix:
Choose one and record it:
(a) v1 definers count in the outer block, run the command in an inner BEGIN…EXCEPTION block, and return the error envelope with response.status set (the mechanism §4.10 already plans for 202), so the count commits.
(b) State that the database counts committed requests only, name an outer limiter for rejected requests (Edge or platform), and add a §12 verify item.
Either way, replays still never count.

findings.reason: The actor key's own foreign keys are not stated. If private.actors.id referenced auth.users the way profiles does (member_core.sql:7, ON DELETE CASCADE), erasure step 6 would cascade into actors and be blocked by every RESTRICT reference. With RESTRICT or NO ACTION it would block step 6 directly.
findings.fix: State that actors.id has no foreign key to auth.users or profiles. Create the actor row no later than the profile, in the same transaction, so no actor reference can come before it.

findings.reason: Per-kind permission (step 7) comes after replay (step 4). A demoted staff member, as opposed to a revoked one, can still replay their own stored outcome for a kind their current role may not issue, and operation_result_v1 (steps 1–2 only) returns it too. Today freeze_action checks per-kind permission before replay (20261019140839_freeze_preview_binding.sql:22, then :24-27), and gym and freeze outcomes still carry balances (checkpoint F-17). The exposure is the same actor's earlier result, so this is acceptable once outcomes are trimmed, but the record does not say so. This does not reopen F1, which concerned revoked scope and is fixed.
findings.fix: In §4.3, state that a demoted actor may replay their own outcome, and that this is accepted only because §4.4 trims outcomes to identifiers. G17.api keeps freeze_action's current order until those outcomes are trimmed.

findings.reason: The checkpoint only asks the package owner to 'consider' failing closed in CI, which is inconsistent with T4. 003 §8 says pnpm check fails when history differs from a Git baseline and that CI sets the variable. The existing mobile-ci.yml runs pnpm check without it.
findings.fix: Record failing closed in CI as a decision (P2A-1). Until PL-1 sets the variable, state in 003 §8 that CI checks no baseline.

findings.fix: Add the review to docs/evidence/AR-1/phase1-review.json on this branch and cite that path.

new_decisions_check.retained_actor_keys: Sound: append-only rows are never updated, actor references use RESTRICT, the gym link uses SET NULL as PRD:1406 requires, and the purge order is explicit. Defects: the tombstone register (PR-1) and the unstated actor foreign keys (PR-3)
new_decisions_check.privacy_notes: PASS. Staff-only notes and tags, my_gym_card_v1, removal of register_read's linked-member branch and exclusion from export are recorded. Both leak paths are cited correctly (gym_operations.sql:108; gym_read_models.sql:137)
new_decisions_check.replay_auth: PASS for revocation: scope comes before lock and replay, and operation_result_v1 is scoped. Note PR-4 on demotion
new_decisions_check.cursor_commit_order: PASS. A per-account counter row is updated in the writing transaction under READ COMMITTED, and its lock is held until commit, so a later commit always gets a higher change_seq than any visible one. The per-link counter on gym_members is consistent with existing FOR UPDATE locks (gym_read_models.sql:24; freeze_preview_binding.sql:19)
new_decisions_check.revocable_objects: PASS. Each bucket's residual is stated. gym-documents and passport grants go through a proxy that rechecks access on every request, deletion purges objects, and the proxy's limits are in §12
new_decisions_check.rate_windows: Mostly sound: read counting no longer depends on READ ONLY transactions, the counter table is UNLOGGED, and replays are excluded. Gap: rejected requests are never counted (PR-2)
